chunks: 32 – Muḥammad ibn Baḥr, al-Ranī, al-Shaybānī, Abū al-Ḥusayn, al-Narmāshīrī.
Weak, in his madhhab there is irtifāʿ.

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعٌ: Irtifāʿ (a technical term in Shia hadith sciences, often referring to elevation in status or a specific doctrinal position, here linked to his weakness)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (in terms of hadith narration reliability)

ai.seo_question: Who is Muḥammad ibn Baḥr al-Narmāshīrī and what is the meaning of 'irtifāʿ' in his madhhab?
ai.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Muhammad ibn Bah'r al-Narmashiri as a weak narrator, a classification that in Shia hadith sciences often implies minor defects in memory or precision rather than doctrinal error. The note on 'irtifa' (elevation) likely refers to his specific theological stance or perhaps a physical characteristic, but in the context of *du'afa*, it serves to distinguish his specific mode of narration or belief from the mainstream Ja'fari school, highlighting the nuanced criteria used by Shia scholars to evaluate the reliability of individual transmitters.

en.tashayyu: 32 – Muḥammad b. Baḥr, al-Ruhanī, al-Shaybānī, Abū al-Ḥusayn, al-Narmāshīrī.
Weak, in his madhhab there is irtifāʿ.
